newsitem.title: USA: Electroglas says seeing unexpected orders.
newsitem.headline: Electroglas says seeing unexpected orders.

text.p: Electroglas Inc president Curtis Wozniak said on Wednesday the company is seeing new orders it did not expect and a healthy uptick in order volume generally.
"We have seen a big turnaround in the marketplace since November, including December, January and February," Wozniak told the Robertson, Stephens & Co technology conference.
"We've even been seeing orders come in that were completely unexpected," he said. "We think 1997 will be a big uptick."
Wozniak said the semiconductor processing equipment manufacturer's book-to-bill ratio is "looking better" than the fourth quarter's 1.3 ratio.
A 1.3 book-to-bill indicates new orders were worth 130 percent of sales billed that quarter.

Analyst Michael Murphy of the California Technology Stock Letter said Electroglas' news about strong orders and similar statements from other semiconductor equipment makers suggests that the equipment industry is turning upward about six months earlier than Wall Street expected.

The semiconductor equipment industry suffered a downturn followed by about six months the downturn in the semiconductor industry. Now it is following the semiconductor industry in experiencing an upturn.
